subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should workspace/internal hooks gain an observation-only outbound `message:sending` event, and if so is the canonical contract colon-only after typed policy, or must `message_sending` remain a supported alias?
rationale: Current docs reserve rewrite and cancellation policy for typed plugin hooks, while this PR creates a new internal event and repository-wide alias rule; code review cannot safely choose that public hook contract.

options.title: Post-policy colon event
options.body: Add an observation-only `message:sending` event after typed rewrite and cancellation, normalizing any approved legacy underscore spelling once without duplicate dispatch.

options.title: Support both spellings
options.body: Treat both spellings as public compatibility aliases, document precedence and de-duplication, and prove existing dual registrations do not fire twice.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Do not add the internal outbound event and direct filtering, rewriting, or cancellation users to the typed plugin-hook surface.

recommendation.title: Post-policy colon event
recommendation.body: Add an observation-only `message:sending` event after typed rewrite and cancellation, normalizing any approved legacy underscore spelling once without duplicate dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: Their maintainer-associated adjacent PR already owns the exact-once and channel-boundary design for `message_sending`.
